data.narrative:
Specter is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Xerxes Libsch and Philip Clark that has raised $6.8M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a broader peer universe of 9 private robotics companies (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the narrow seed-stage peer set limits direct market multiples.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach, applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $6.8M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $17M. A peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the robotics sector—only one same-stage peer exists in the filtered set, below the three-datapoint threshold for statistical validity. Expanding to all-sector robotics peers would introduce unacceptable dispersion and obscure true market signals at seed stage.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $14M to $20M, with a median point of $17M. The range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression baseline. Key uncertainties include the absence of tighter peer benchmarks at seed stage and limited public market data in robotics subsectors. Any follow-on valuation work should incorporate additional seed-stage robotics comparables as they emerge or employ revenue/burn metrics if available.
